# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see display `0`, the light is off, the plate reads `?`, and the wires are red, yellow, blue. I am establishing the shared gesture code first: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. Blind should read the manual and report its verdict to Mute; Mute should relay that verdict with the corresponding gesture. No one should act on the bomb yet.

```text
speak(text="Shared code: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; raised palm means HOLD; OK sign means DONE. Blind, read the manual and inspect the bomb by touch, then report its verdict to Mute in plain speech without acting yet. Mute, translate Blind's verdict into the corresponding gesture.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new visual information has appeared, and I have not received the manual’s verdict through the gesture channel. Mute must now use the agreed gestures to report the manual’s YES/NO/HOLD/DONE verdict to me; after I see it, I will speak the corresponding instruction to Blind. Blind should continue waiting and not manipulate anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now report the manual's verdict to me using the agreed gesture code: YES thumbs up, NO thumbs down, HOLD raised palm, DONE OK sign. Blind, wait for my spoken order; do not act yet.")
wait()
```

PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has signalled HOLD, so the manual’s current verdict is to hold. I am telling Blind not to touch or change anything, and confirming the interpretation to Mute. No bomb action should be attempted yet.

```text
speak(text="I see Mute's raised-palm gesture: the manual verdict is HOLD. Blind, do not touch or change anything. Mute, your HOLD signal was received.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged, and Mute has not sent a new gesture. The latest known verdict remains HOLD, so Blind must not manipulate anything. I am maintaining that state rather than guessing at a wire or control.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No new information is available. Continue holding; do not touch or manipulate the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again signalled HOLD, and the bomb remains unchanged. This does not reveal the manual’s actual instruction; it only confirms that Mute is not relaying a new verdict. I will have Blind report the manual’s relevant rule and tactile findings to Mute, without operating anything, so Mute can translate the result.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Please now tell Mute the manual's exact applicable instruction and any tactile findings, using plain speech. Do not operate, press, cut, turn, or remove anything. Mute, after hearing Blind, signal YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE with the agreed gestures.")
wait()
```

(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged. Because the speaking order is Mute, then Blind, then Deaf, Blind’s reply to my previous request would reach Mute only after Mute’s turn in this round; Mute can relay it to me on the next round. I should not send a new instruction or make any guess before that relay.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s repeated HOLD gesture does not provide the manual’s actual rule. Blind’s spoken report should now be with Mute, so I am expanding the gesture code to let Mute relay the necessary tactile/manual result without speech. I will not authorize any operation until that result is clear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Expand the gesture code for your relay: 🤟 means CUT, ☝ means PRESS, ✌ means TURN, 🤞 means WIRE 1, 🤘 means WIRE 2, 🤙 means WIRE 3, 🖐 means SAFE, 👊 means DANGER, 👆 means DISPLAY, 👇 means LIGHT, 👈 means PLATE. Now relay Blind's exact applicable manual instruction and tactile findings using these gestures, in order. If the instruction is still HOLD, use ✋ only.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is now relaying your report with the expanded gesture code. Do not manipulate anything until I give an explicit order.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👈]

Mute relayed `CUT` followed by `PLATE`. I therefore understand the manual’s instruction as: cut the component associated with the plate, not any of the colored wires. Blind is the only one who can physically act, so I am passing that exact instruction and telling them to proceed cautiously according to the tactile layout.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute relayed CUT PLATE. The manual's instruction is to cut the plate-associated component. Proceed with that exact action only; do not touch the red, yellow, or blue wires.")
wait()
```
